text:
mia: quick bring-up for jigsaw-v0.9 int6 onboarding — ran multi-domain holdout eval, and we're seeing a noticeable recall@1 drop vs the float baseline. sharing the fast summary below.

embed-bot: automatic eval results attached.
embed-bot: model=jigsaw-v0.9-int6 | index=hnsw | normalize=true | k=[1,5,10] | recall@1=0.71 | recall@5=0.89 | recall@10=0.93 | silhouette=-0.02 | baseline_recall@1=0.78 | baseline_silhouette=0.12

raj: can you paste the exact eval command? also did you use whitening / PCA? those shifts often come from mismatch in centering.

mia: command was: ```
./eval_embeddings.py --model jigsaw-v0.9-int6 --holdout multi_domain --k 1,5,10 --index hnsw --normalize true --whiten false
```

sofia: interesting — the silhouette drop suggests cluster separability degraded, not just a global scale shift. did you check per-domain recall? maybe one domain is tanking.

embed-bot: per-domain recall snippet: news: r@1 0.74 -> 0.80, docs: r@1 0.65 -> 0.78, qa: r@1 0.78 -> 0.77. looks like "docs" domain primarily impacted.

drew: docs often have short queries + heavy stopwords. int6 per-channel quantization sometimes amplifies differences for small-norm vectors. try per-channel vs symmetric per-tensor and also test L2-normalize before/after quant.

mia: scheduling a quick matrix: [per-channel,int6] vs [per-tensor,int6] vs [int8 baseline] and whiten true/false. also want to try index params: efSearch and M variations.

sofia: can you also run a UMAP scatter for docs holdout? would like to eyeball cluster overlap. if clusters overlap heavily for docs, it explains recall collapse.

mia: putting the UMAP link here: https://redwood.artifacts/umap/jigsaw-v0.9-int6-docs-umap.png 

raj: thanks — looking at that, I can see the doc anchors merging into a dense cloud. two quick checks: 1) compare query-length distribution between baseline and int6 eval sets (maybe tokenization changed), 2) make sure we didn't accidentally strip contextual tokens during preprocessing.

embed-bot: quick stats: avg_query_len_tokens baseline=14.2 | int6_eval=13.9; median is same. no obvious tokenization mismatch found in sample of 1000.

drew: add a micro-batch test too — batching can change KV-cache dynamics on serve-time, which sometimes surfaces as subtle embedding drift in our offline sim harness. run with batch sizes 1,8,32.

mia: noted. i'll kick off the matrix now on the canary nodes and share logs. expected results ETA ~45m.

ops-bot: rerun scheduled on canary cluster: canary-3 at 04:30 UTC. job id r-1764141414-1. will post results to this thread when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sofia: thanks! once we have the matrix, we should compute per-query delta to identify worst-off queries and add them to the regression promptset if needed.

mia: agreed — plan is: rerun matrix, collect per-query deltas, surface top 200 worst queries, and decide whether to adjust quant profile or fallback to int8 for docs domain.

raj: awesome. ping me if you want help crafting the regression promptset or running stratified kfold recall checks.

mia: will do. moving this to follow-up when results land. :pray:
